title: Deployment Watchtower — multi-signal alarm scoring and auto-evacuation
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Goal: Build a multi-signal alarm scoring service ("Watchtower") that evaluates canary/A-B/shadow traffic against configured SLOs (p95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, tokens/sec throughput) and escalates automatically along a staged response path: notify -> divert traffic -> isolate model variant -> auto-evacuate (rollback).

Motivation: Current canary checks are per-metric hard thresholds which either miss regressions in correlated signals or trigger too-often due to noisy metrics. Watchtower will combine signals into a single, explainable score with tunable sensitivity and cohort-aware baselines so we reduce false positives and catch multi-dimensional regressions (e.g., slightly higher latency + higher token churn).

High-level design:
- Ingest metric streams (prometheus/cortex + Redwood runtime telemetry) and event metadata (model id, version, route, cohort) into a short-term evaluation window.
- Compute per-signal standardized deltas vs. baseline (z-score-like), apply per-signal weightings configured per-project.
- Aggregate into a composite risk score and run against per-rollout policy bands (warning/partial-divert/evacuate).
- Implement hysteresis, minimum-eval-window, minimum-requests thresholds, and cohort partitioning to avoid spuriously triggering on small cohorts.
- Provide API and console hooks for human review, manual overrides, and audit logging.

Trade-offs considered:
- Rule-based vs model-based detection: start with explainable weighted aggregation (fast to iterate, auditable) and keep a telemetry pipeline to evaluate ML anomaly detectors as a follow-up.
- Global threshold vs cohort baselines: choose cohort-aware baselines by default for customer-sensitive workloads to reduce false positives from traffic mix changes.
- Auto-evacuation risk: require multi-signal agreement and minimum sample size; auto-evacuation reserved for high-confidence, high-impact degradations.

Operational constraints: must work within 1s evaluation latency for canaries with real-time dashboards and must not add significant runtime overhead to the serving path (metrics-only, no sync calls on inference path).
acceptance_criteria: Composite risk score computed for every active canary rollout and visible in console within 1s of metric ingestion
Policy bands configurable per-project and per-model with default presets for low/medium/high sensitivity
Auto-evacuation executes only when: composite score > evacuation threshold, sample_size >= configured_min, and at least two signals cross their pr thresholds
Audit logs created for every automated action including metric snapshots and decision rationale
End-to-end integration test: simulated latency and token-cost regressions in canary traffic cause staged response (notify -> partial diversion -> evacuation) in test harness
Runbook and incident playbook created for false positive events and manual remediation steps
comments: 2025-02-18 - Aisha Khatri: Created ticket. Initial spike attached: evaluated Prometheus vs. direct runtime pushes for short-window evaluation. Decided to prototype with Cortex ingestion to avoid runtime coupling.
2025-02-21 - Tomás Rivera: POC aggregator implemented (branch gh/infra/watchtower-POC). Uses sliding 60s window, z-score per-signal, simple weighted sum. Pushed metrics export to staging-cortex.

2025-02-25 - Maria Li (PM): Reviewed POC. Feedback: include token-cost as first-class signal and expose sensitivity presets (conservative/standard/aggressive). Also request ability to pin cohorts for experiments.

2025-03-01 - Security review note (S. Patel): No secrets in pipeline; audit logging requirement noted. Confirmed that auto-evacuation will require two-person approval for enterprise tenants (configurable).

2025-03-03 - Engineering review (infra): Added minimum-sample-size gating and cohort partitioning to prevent small-cohort flapping. Performance: aggregator uses ~120ms CPU per evaluation in staging under 200 concurrent canaries.

2025-03-05 - Tomás Rivera: Submitted draft RFC for review: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Deployment+Watchtower (Design + Policy examples). Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1456
2025-03-05 - UX/Console (L. Gomez): Prototype panel for Watchtower scoring added to console CANARY tab. Request: show top contributing signals in tooltip and link to raw metric traces.
notes: Next steps: finalize policy DSL for weighting and band definitions; implement dry-run mode for 2 weeks to collect false-positive / true-positive stats; add enterprise guardrail requiring 2 approvals for auto-evacuation by default
Follow-ups: evaluate ML anomaly detector (ENG-69011) once baseline data collected; add cost-aware policies to allow benign token-cost increases within budget windows
Related incident: INC-2025-11 referenced in design doc motivated adding token-cost signal after spike in token churn during beta rollout
